step1_analysis.description: A regenerative frequency divider that uses a cross-coupled NMOS pair to provide negative resistance for an LC tank, and parallel NMOS transistors to inject the input signal. It divides the input frequency by 2 by locking the oscillator to half the injection frequency.

paper_reference.title: A 40-GHz Frequency Divider in 0.18-m CMOS Technology

division_ratio.description: The ratio of the input frequency to the output frequency.

sky130_expected.calculation: Determined by the circuit topology (regenerative divider).
sky130_expected.reasoning: The fundamental operation of this Miller/regenerative divider topology is divide-by-2.

input_frequency.description: The frequency of the input signal that the circuit can successfully divide.

sky130_expected.calculation: Targeted for 10 GHz in the testbench using a 5 GHz resonant LC tank (L=1nH, C=1pF).
sky130_expected.reasoning: While the paper achieved 40 GHz in 180nm, the provided netlist has relatively long channels (L=0.5u) and small widths (W=5u). A 10 GHz input (5 GHz output) is a more realistic target for these specific transistor dimensions in SKY130.

power_consumption.description: Total DC power consumed by the circuit from the supply.

sky130_expected.calculation: I_tail ≈ 0.5 * u_n * C_ox * (W/L) * (V_GS - V_TH)^2. For W=5u, L=0.5u, V_GS=1.0V, V_TH=0.42V: I_tail ≈ 0.5 * 270u * 10 * (0.58)^2 ≈ 0.45 mA per tail. Total current ≈ 0.9 mA. Power = 1.8V * 0.9mA = 1.62 mW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The paper's 31 mW implies much larger transistors and higher bias currents to achieve 40 GHz. The provided netlist's small W/L ratios will consume significantly less power.

output_voltage_swing.description: Peak-to-peak voltage amplitude of the divided output signal.

sky130_expected.calculation: V_swing ≈ I_tail * R_tank. With I_tail = 0.45 mA and R_tank = 1k ohm, single-ended swing is roughly 0.45V peak, or 0.9V peak-to-peak.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends heavily on the Q-factor and parallel resistance of the LC tank used as the load.

step3_testbench.description: Transient analysis to verify divide-by-2 operation at 10 GHz input frequency. Measures the output frequency, voltage swing, and average power consumption. An LC tank resonant at 5 GHz is added as the load.
step3_testbench.spice:
* ILFD Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u
.param W_xm6=5u L_xm6=0.5u

XM1 N_S1 N_G1 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 N_S2 N_G2 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 VOUT_L VIN_P N_S1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 VOUT_L VOUT_R N_S1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM5 VOUT_R VOUT_L N_S2 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}
XM6 VOUT_R VIN_N N_S2 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm6} w={W_xm6}

* LC Tank Loads (Resonant at ~5 GHz)
L1 VDD VOUT_L 1n
C1 VOUT_L 0 1p
R1 VDD VOUT_L 1k

L2 VDD VOUT_R 1n
C2 VOUT_R 0 1p
R2 VDD VOUT_R 1k

* DC Sources
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VBIAS1 N_G1 0 1.0
VBIAS2 N_G2 0 1.0

* 10 GHz Differential Input Signal
VVIN_P VIN_P 0 DC 0.9 SIN(0.9 0.5 10G 0 0 0)
VVIN_N VIN_N 0 DC 0.9 SIN(0.9 0.5 10G 0 0 180)

.control
tran 2p 5n

* Measure output frequency (period between 10th and 11th rising edge)
meas tran t_period trig v(VOUT_L) val=1.8 rise=10 targ v(VOUT_L) val=1.8 rise=11
let fout = 1 / t_period
print fout

* Measure output voltage swing
meas tran vout_max max v(VOUT_L) from=3n to=5n
meas tran vout_min min v(VOUT_L) from=3n to=5n
let vout_swing = vout_max - vout_min
print vout_swing

* Measure power consumption
meas tran pwr avg i(VVDD) from=3n to=5n
let power = -pwr * 1.8
print power

quit
.endc
